tagline.text: A day of white sandbars and palm islets linked by outrigger boat

location.label: Location
location.text: Surigao del Norte Province, off General Luna (Guyam, Daku and Naked Islands)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–2,500 per person (one island hopping tour)

children.text: This is Siargao's signature island hopping trip: a single day by outrigger boat to Naked Island, a white sandbar off General Luna, Daku Island with its broad palm-fringed beach, and Guyam Island, a tiny postcard-perfect islet. The boat rides are short, leaving plenty of time to swim, take photos and enjoy a seafood lunch.

Just off General Luna, the main town on Siargao, lie three small islands that you can see in half a day by outrigger boat (bangka). They are Naked Island, a bare white sandbar (known locally as Pansukian); Daku Island, with coconut palms lining its beach; and Guyam Island, a very small islet packed with palm trees. Visiting all three in one day is the famous three-island hopping tour, and it is the first activity we recommend even to travelers who do not surf.
The three islands have very different characters. Naked Island is less an island than a sandbar that emerges inside the reef, only about
long, with not a single tree and clear water on every side. Daku is the largest of the three, home to a few families, and offers huts, meals and palm shade. Guyam is an uninhabited islet about
long and
wide, with an area of roughly
, lying about
2km
south-southeast of central General Luna.
The short distances are the big advantage of this route. Crossing between islands from the General Luna pier takes roughly
15–30 minutes
per leg, so most tours leave in the morning and return by mid-afternoon. With so little time spent traveling, you can stay
1–2 hours
on each island to swim, take photos and have lunch, which makes it easy for first-time island hoppers, families and couples.
This entry focuses on the island hopping tour rather than the whole of Siargao. If you are curious about surf breaks, Sugba Lagoon or the land tours of the north of the island, see the
Siargao

entry as well. Here we cover the best order for visiting, what to do and watch out for on each island, and how tour costs add up. The look of the islands and whether boats run both depend on the tide and weather, so confirm with your operator once more the day before.

The size of the sandbar changes with the tide, and it is a place for photos that look like walking between sky and sea. There is no shade at all, the sun is strong and the current is fairly swift, so it is safer to play in the water and take photos along the edge of the sandbar than to swim out into deeper water. Most visitors stay for about
1 hour

This is the widest of the three islands and its sand is soft. Palm shade runs along the beach, so it feels less crowded even when many people are there, and the water shades from pale turquoise in the shallows to deep navy farther out. The sight of bangkas lined up along the beach is the island's trademark.

You rent a hut run by local residents and have freshly caught fish, shrimp and shellfish grilled for lunch. Whether lunch is included in the tour price varies by operator, so check when you book, and a fresh coconut drink makes the midday heat much easier to bear.

Even at a leisurely pace, you can walk around the island in a few minutes. One side is a white sand beach and the other a rocky shoreline, so the mood differs within one small island. Drinks are sold on the beach, which makes it a pleasant place to rest, and some travelers come to watch the sunset.

blocks.title: Swimming and snorkeling in clear water

children.text: On all three islands the boat drops you into waist-deep, transparent water. Ask the boatman which beach is easiest for swimming that day, since it depends on the current, and if you rent or bring snorkeling gear you can see shallow coral and small tropical fish.

blocks.title: Watching the surf break at Daku Island

children.text: The waters around Daku Island have gentler waves than Cloud 9 and are known as a place where beginners go. Even if you do not surf, you can watch people riding boards on the sea. If you want to add a surf session to your hopping day, ask the operator in advance whether it is possible.

On days with good weather and calm seas, some travelers paddle a kayak all the way to the islands. Because of currents and boat traffic, try it only if you are a strong swimmer with sea experience, and always carry safety equipment and a life jacket.

blocks.title: Planning the route around the tide

children.text: The shape of the islands changes greatly with the tide. If you set the order so that you visit Naked Island when the sandbar is widely exposed, your photos will look their best. Ask the boatman about the tide the day before and he can adjust the order of the stops.
Have breakfast at your accommodation and pack sunscreen, a hat, a towel and a waterproof bag.
Meet your guide at the General Luna pier, put on a life jacket and board the bangka.
Arrive at Naked Island and walk the sandbar and take photos for about
1 hour
Move to Daku Island to swim and relax on the beach.
Have a grilled seafood lunch at a hut on Daku Island.
Move to Guyam Island, walk around it and play in the water.
Return to the pier, then shower and rest at your accommodation.
Departure times and the order of stops differ slightly by operator. The boatman may also change the order depending on the tide and wind.

items.title: Relaxed afternoon route
items.subtitle: Half a day, aimed at sunset

children.text: Eat a late lunch and head to the pier.
Arrive at Daku Island, swim and stroll along the beach.
Move to Guyam Island and relax with a drink.
Return to the pier before sunset.
Whether you can stay until sunset depends on the operator and the weather. Be sure to confirm the return time when you book.

items.title: Two-day combination
items.subtitle: Island hopping plus another boat tour

children.text: Enjoy the three-island hopping tour.
Rest at your accommodation or take a surf lesson.
Spend the day on another boat tour such as
Sohoton Cove
or a land tour of the island.
Island hopping can be cancelled when the sea is rough, so if you stay two days or more, book the hopping day first and keep a spare day.

Flight arrangements from Manila to Siargao (Sayak Airport, IAO) have changed often. Because turboprop routes have been shifting toward Clark Airport, travelers from Manila generally connect through Cebu or fly direct from Clark. Flight time is about
1 hour to 2 hours 30 minutes
depending on the route, and fares are about
one way, though they rise sharply in peak season. Check the latest schedules before booking.
If air tickets are expensive or sold out, you can go through Surigao City. From Surigao port to Dapa port on Siargao, take a fast ferry (about
1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours
) or a RoRo ferry (about
3–4 hours
), then continue from Dapa to General Luna by van or tricycle in about
30–40 minutes
. Ferries are cancelled in bad weather, so leave extra time before your flight home.

items.title: From the airport to General Luna

children.text: A shared van from Sayak Airport to General Luna takes about
45 minutes to 1 hour
and costs about
per person. If you arrange a hotel pickup, you pay one vehicle fare. The hopping pier is in central General Luna, close to most accommodations.

There are three ways to book. You can haggle directly with a boatman near the pier, join a package sold by your hotel or resort, or pay in advance on an online tour booking site. Haggling lets a group share a chartered boat, which works out better the more people you have, while joining a package is easier for first-time visitors who do not want to bargain. Either way, check whether lunch, life jackets and island entrance fees are included.
Siargao faces the Pacific directly, so rain is frequent, and hopping tours run only when the sea is calm. From
November
to
February
the northeast monsoon brings plenty of rain and high waves, and some days hopping is cancelled. From
March
to
May
the sea is calmest and the sky clear, making it the best time for island hopping, and hopping is usually possible in
June–October
as well.
Typhoons are rarer here than in other parts of the Philippines, but in
December 2021

Super Typhoon Rai (Odette locally) struck the island and caused heavy damage. The weather can turn suddenly around the year-end holidays, so check forecasts, and rather than hopping on your first day, pick a day when the weather is good.

The easiest base for island hopping is General Luna, where the departure pier is. Around Cloud 9 and Tourism Road you will find hostels (dorm beds about
per night), guesthouses (about

per night) and resorts, and the pier is a short scooter or tricycle ride away. Many tours leave very early, so check whether hotel pickup is included. Around the year-end holidays and in peak season, rooms fill early and prices rise sharply.

There are almost no restaurants on the islands, so you rely on the lunch included in the tour. On Daku you get fish, shrimp and shellfish grilled over charcoal, rice and fresh coconut drinks. On Guyam, drinks are sold on the beach. After hopping, many travelers have dinner in General Luna, with grilled fish and seafood kinilaw at a carinderia, or smoothie bowls and café food.
Before booking, ask whether the tour price includes lunch, life jackets, snorkel gear and island entrance fees, and carry plenty of cash. Cards are often not accepted on the islands.
There is no shade on Naked Island. Bring a hat, a rash guard, reef-safe sunscreen and sunglasses, and drink plenty of water.
The seabed has a lot of coral and it is easy to hurt your feet, so wear water shoes. Do not step on or touch the coral.
Choose a tour that leaves in the morning, when the water color is clearest, and if possible go on a weekday when there are fewer people.
Put your camera and phone in a waterproof bag. Getting splashed or wet by waves while boarding and leaving the boat is common.
Take your trash back with you and cut down on single-use plastic. The environment of a small island is easily damaged.
The day before, ask the boatman about the tide and wind, and if the weather is bad, postpone to another day.
When you haggle for a chartered boat, settle the islands to visit, the time spent, the return time and whether lunch is included before departure, and fix the price.

Naked Island has no shade and a fairly strong current. In the daytime it is easy to get sunburned or dehydrated, so do not swim into deeper water beyond the edge of the sandbar, and wear a life jacket when you play in the water.
On days with a rough sea, hopping can be cancelled or cut short. Do not schedule hopping the day before your flight home.
Scrapes from coral reef easily become infected. If you get a wound, rinse it with clean water and disinfect it at once. General Luna has small clinics.
Avoid boats that carry more passengers than they should, and check before departure that you are wearing your life jacket.
Rules on visitor numbers, hours and fees at the islands may change, so check the latest notices when you book.
Leave valuables at your accommodation and keep them in a waterproof bag on the islands.
Find information on the whole island, including the Cloud 9 boardwalk and surf lessons in General Luna, Sugba Lagoon and the Magpupungko rock pools.
